title: The Metamorphosis
text:
Gregor Samsa, a traveling salesman, woke one morning to find himself transformed into a huge insect. His first worry was not his new body but that he would miss his train and lose his job. For years he had worked at a job he hated to pay off his parents' debts and support the family, and he had dreamed of sending his sister Grete to study the violin.

When the family saw him, his mother fainted and his father drove him back into his room with a stick. At first Grete brought him food and cleaned his room. But the family soon had to find work themselves: the father as a bank messenger, the mother sewing, Grete as a shop girl. They took in lodgers. Gregor's room became a storeroom for junk.

Once, when Gregor came out, his father pelted him with apples. One lodged in his back and rotted there. When Gregor crept out to listen to Grete playing the violin for the lodgers, they saw him and gave notice. Grete told her parents that they must get rid of it. That thing could not be Gregor, she said; if it were, he would have gone away on his own.

That night Gregor died, thinking of his family with tenderness. The next morning the family took the day off, rode a tram into the country, and noticed with pleasure that Grete had grown into a pretty young woman ready to marry.
lesson: A family member is worth more than what he or she provides. Pay attention if your love for someone depends on how useful they are to you.
people: Gregor Samsa, his parents, his sister Grete
